title: 7 Best missed call text back software for businesses
summary: Sick of playing phone tag? Worried about frustrating your customers? Here are seven missed call text back software options you can use.
body_markdown:
What’s more annoying than[missing a business call](https://www.quo.com/product/call-management/never-miss-a-call) ? Missing *two* business calls — and maybe more. Studies show that most businesses miss[nearly a quarter](https://www.invoca.com/blog/how-many-phone-calls-are-you-missing) of their incoming calls. This could result in hundreds of lost opportunities — not to mention potential customers.


But these days, you don’t need to stay glued to your phone to prevent losing customers. With missed call text back software, you can instantly respond to unanswered calls with an automated text.


This guide compares the best missed call text back software so you can choose the right fit for your business. Once we compare the pros, cons, and features, we list their plans and pricing so you can make an informed decision.


##


What is missed call text back software?


**


Missed call text back software sends automatic messages to callers if no one on your team picks up the phone. That way, you can set expectations about when you’ll be back and give callers instructions on what to do in the meantime.


##

Not all text-back solutions are created equal. Some are bare-bones apps that send basic replies. Others are full business phone systems with text-back as one feature among many.


**Key differences to watch for:**


- **Integration capabilities** — Can it work with your existing CRM and the rest of your tech stack?
- **Team collaboration** — Can multiple people handle conversations and share numbers?
- **Customization options** — How much control do you have over messages and timing?
- **Scalability** — Will it grow with your business or limit you?


Let’s start with the #1 solution in customer satisfaction as rated by G2:


### **1. Quo: The best solution for small businesses and growing teams**


Quo, formerly OpenPhone, is a cloud-based phone system designed to help businesses grow and scale. Every member of your team gets their own local or toll-free number so they can make and receive unlimited texts in the US and Canada.


With Quo, you can send personalized auto-replies to customers if you miss their calls or texts, such as calls on the weekend or[during holidays](https://www.quo.com/blog/holiday-text-messages/) . You can also set up different messages depending on whether customers:


- Call during or after hours
- Leave a voicemail, or not
- Leave a text message


Worried about spamming your customers with messages? This won’t be a problem with Quo. We only send one auto-reply every three hours to the same contact. This means you don’t have to worry about overwhelming customers with texts if they contact you multiple times within a three-hour period.


You can also cut down on missed calls by[using one phone number on two phones](https://www.quo.com/blog/how-to-use-one-phone-number-on-two-phones/) — or sharing a number. With shared numbers, every member of the number is notified of incoming calls and texts. This means there’s almost always someone around to pick up the phone.


You can also avoid missing calls by using[Sona](https://www.quo.com/sona) , Quo’s[AI voice agent](https://www.quo.com/product/ai/voice-agent) that can take calls during or after hours. Sona can:


- Answer common questions based on the information you provide and take messages 24/7.
- Automatically record and log calls. Sona also includes a call transcript and summary so you can easily follow up on conversations.
- Send SMS messages during live calls. For example, Sona can text callers a booking link. This lets them schedule an appointment on their own instead of waiting for a follow-up call from one of your reps.


If you miss calls or want to filter by calls taken by Sona, you can check Quo’s call views to identify the customers you missed calls from. This allows you to get context quickly and prioritize the calls that need immediate action.


You can also access Quo from any device, whether you prefer our mobile app, web browser, or desktop app. We designed our platform to be simple and intuitive so you can get up and running in 15 minutes or less.


Want to put this to the test?[Sign up for a free trial of Quo](https://my.quo.com/signup) today.


#### **Quo pricing**


Quo offers three different pricing plans for you to choose from:


- **Starter** : $15 per user per month for unlimited auto-replies, shared phone numbers, third-party integrations, and more
- **Business** : $23 per user per month for[AI contact suggestions](https://www.quo.com/product/ai/suggested-contacts) , customizable ring orders, advanced call forwarding, CRM integrations, and more
- **Scale** : $35 per user per month for AI call tags, dedicated onboarding support, inbound phone support, and priority live chat and email support


### **2. Grasshopper: Best for multi-digit extensions**


[Grasshopper](https://www.quo.com/blog/grasshopper-alternatives/) is a legacy VoIP provider that lets you put[multi-digit extensions](https://www.quo.com/blog/phone-extension/) on your reps’ phone numbers. This gives you plenty of options for missed call management. For example, you can record custom greetings on every extension and set up call forwarding to other numbers. Plus, you’ll be able to receive voicemail transcriptions to your email address, letting you quickly get context on missed calls.


Like Quo, Grasshopper allows you to automatically send texts to missed calls so you can set expectations about when you’ll respond. Unfortunately, they’re more limited tha Quo’s tools, which could negatively affect your customer’s experience.


For example, you can’t send automatic missed call texts if a caller:


- Leaves a voicemail on your number
- Hangs up before they dial an extension
- Has called your business before


But that’s not the worst of Grasshopper’s limitations. For example, its international calling comes with several restrictions. You’ll need to put down a $500 deposit to make international calls. Plus, your account needs to be 60 days old, or five days if you’re based in Hawaii or Alaska.


#### Grasshopper pricing


**


[Grasshopper’s pricing plans](https://www.quo.com/blog/grasshopper-pricing/) give you three different options:


- **True Solo:** $14 per month for one number, one extension, and one user
- **Solo Plus:** $25 per month for one number, three extensions, and unlimited users
- **Small Business:** $55 per month for four phone numbers, unlimited extensions, and unlimited users


### **3. Allo: Best for unlimited international calling**


[Allo](https://www.quo.com/blog/allo-alternatives/) is a business phone system that supports desktop and mobile apps on its base plan. Your team can answer calls and messages from their computer or phone, whether they’re at their desk or out on a job.


You can also connect Allo to Shopify so you can see helpful customer information before picking up the phone. For example, Allo will display the customer’s name, order history, lifetime spending, and any active orders on your phone’s screen when they call.


If you need a presence in specific European countries, you can purchase French and Swiss numbers. Plus, the app lets you make unlimited calls to 47 destinations, making it easier to support global customers.


While these features may look appealing, the base plan has several limitations. Keep in mind, you can only text if you upgrade to their Business plan, starting at $32 per user per month. Even if you upgrade, your team can only send 150 SMS messages per day. After that, you’ll pay $0.01 per SMS message and $0.03 per MMS message.


#### Allo pricing


**


Allo lets you choose from two different pricing plans:


- **Solo** : $120 for one user per year for unlimited calls in the US and Canada, business hours, and call recording
- **Business** : $32 per user per month for texting, click to call, AI call summaries, and call analytics
- **Ultra** : $100 per user per month for custom analytics dashboards, custom AI voice for your IVR, access to Slack support, SLA, and granular admin controls


### **4. Enzak: Best missed call text back software for enterprises**


Enzak is a customer engagement app that instantly responds to missed calls with texts. Like Quo, it has text message templates you can use to quickly answer frequently asked questions.


With Enzak, you can tap into detailed analytics that list metrics, such as your click-through rates and user locations. You can also integrate with tools you already use, including your[IVR software](https://www.quo.com/blog/ivr-software/) and[phone tree](https://www.quo.com/blog/phone-tree/) service.


But the price you’d pay for an Enzak plan exceeds that of a full[business phone system](https://www.quo.com/blog/best-small-business-phone-systems/) . At $99 per month plus a $99 one-time setup fee, it’s not the most cost-effective solution for growing small businesses. This doesn’t include its add-on costs:


- Visual voicemail is $75 per month
- Call-back requests start at $49 per month
- Sending more than 1,000 text messages per month requires upgrading to its enterprise plan
- [Two-way messages](https://www.quo.com/product/messaging/two-way-sms) cost $49.00 per month


The not-so-great cherry on top? Limited service locations. Enzak only supports customers in the US and Canada. So if you’re located overseas, you’ll need to look for an Enzak alternative.


#### Enzak pricing


**


Enzak publicly lists one pricing tier: $99 per month, plus a $99 one-time fee. This includes 1,000 automated texts and custom templates for after business hours text messages.


Additional costs include:


- Additional users per plan for $10 per user per month
- AI-enhanced visual voicemail for $75 per month
- Call back requests for $49 per month


Enzak *does* offer enterprise-level text message plans, but you have to contact the company directly for a quote.


### **5. Weave: Best for healthcare practices**


[Weave](https://www.quo.com/blog/weave-alternatives/) is a VoIP phone system specifically designed for healthcare practices. Do you operate in plastic surgery, dentistry, veterinary care, or a similar field? Then you’ll be able to tap into a suite of its communication tools, such as Missed Call Texting and Text to Pay.


With Weave, it’s easy to[respond to missed calls by text](https://www.quo.com/blog/how-to-respond-to-a-missed-call-by-text/) with its Missed Call Texting feature. You can also use its Waitlist/ASAP list, which text customers about recent cancellations so they can claim a spot on your calendar.


Unfortunately, the base plan comes with 1,500 messages per month. If you want to send more, you’ll need to upgrade or pay for an add-on. Keep in mind that the pricing for these bundles also isn’t listed publicly. You also can’t use its online scheduling feature without upgrading.


Keep in mind, the only pricing information Weave provides is that its plans start at $199 per month.


You also have to worry about where your business is located. Weave is only available for purchase to customers in the US and Canada. Plus, the company is vague about its international texting features, so you may or may not be able to reach telehealth patients overseas.


#### Weave pricing


**


[Weave’s pricing](https://www.quo.com/blog/weave-pricing/) isn’t public. The only information available is that their base Pro plans start at $199 per month.


You’ll have to contact the company for an accurate quote. Here are the features you can expect to get on each of its plans:


- **Pro** : 1,500 messages, missed call texting, and an overdue patients list
- **Elite** : 3,000 messages, online scheduling, and digital forms
- **Ultimate** : 15,000 messages,[call intelligence](https://www.quo.com/blog/call-intelligence/) , and practice analytics for dental practices only


### **6.HighLevel: Best for lead nurturing**


HighLevel is a sales and marketing platform that agencies can white-label and resell to their clients. It gives you tools to capture leads with websites, funnels, and landing pages. Then, you can nurture those leads with features like video messaging directly from its mobile app.


What if a lead is ready to buy? HighLevel also gives you tools to help close the sale. For example, you can integrate HighLevel with Stripe to accept customer payments.


Plus,[HighLevel](https://www.quo.com/integrations/highlevel) lets you call and text leads. But instead of a flat monthly rate, you’ll pay based on how much you use its phone service:


- **SMS:** $0.00747 per segment for inbound and outbound texts
- **Calls** : $0.0166 per minute to make calls and $0.01165 per minute to receive them
- **Call recording:** $0.0025 per minute
- **Call recording storage:** $0.0005 per minute per month


You should know that these charges also apply when you use HighLevel’s auto missed call text-back feature.


If you want HighLevel’s sales and marketing tools without relying on its phone service, you can connect it with Quo. That way, your HighLevel contacts automatically sync and you don’t have to worry about the fees mentioned above.


#### HighLevel pricing


**


HighLevel provides three different plans to choose from.


- **Starter:** $97 per month for 3 sub-accounts, unlimited contacts, unlimited users, and domain management
- **Unlimited:** $297 per month for unlimited sub-accounts, rebilling phone and email with no markup, and basic API access
- **Agency Pro:** $497 per month for automated sub-account creation, user and agent reporting, and advanced API access


### **7. Podium: Best for omnichannel routing**


[Podium](https://www.quo.com/blog/podium-alternatives/) started as a reputation management solution in 2014. Since then, it’s expanded to include tools for generating and managing leads. It lets you bring customer interactions into one place, so your team can stay on top of leads and follow up before they fall through the cracks.


While Podium offers missed-call text back software, those messages count toward your SMS limit. Go over it, and you’ll need to pay for a monthly add-on. Podium doesn’t publish how much this will cost your business.


But Podium doesn’t publish its pricing. To find out how much it costs, you’ll need to sign up for a demo or talk to a sales rep. One Trustpilot reviewer found the service expensive and said making account changes often required scheduling an appointment with their account manager.


*“They are super expensive for what you get. Almost any modification on your account, you have to schedule an appoinment with your manager. You have little control over what you can do by yourself.”* —[Trustpilot](https://www.trustpilot.com/reviews/6a6a3ced933a35f3458e5781)


#### Podium pricing


**


[Podium’s pricing](https://www.quo.com/blog/podium-pricing/) isn’t public. But here’s what you can expect to get on each plan:


- **Core:** AI review response suggestions, basic reporting, phones systems add-on, and dedicated customer success manager
- **Pro:** AI instant answers, AI review responses, AI phone call summaries, and lead capture forms
- **Signature:** Advanced multi-location management and quarterly business reviews


##


How to select the right missed call text back software for your needs


Missed call text back software can vary quite a bit from one tool to the next. Here are four questions to ask to help you choose the best fit for your business:


1. **Can you customize auto-replies for different situations?** Someone who calls after hours needs a different response than someone who leaves a voicemail during the day. Check whether you can customize messages based on when someone calls and whether they leave a voicemail or have sent a text.
2. **Can multiple team members answer from the same number?** Customers shouldn’t have to wait for one person to become available. Shared numbers give multiple teammates access to the same calls and texts, so whoever’s available can quickly follow up.
3. **Does it prevent repeat auto-replies from feeling like spam?** If a customer calls more than once in a short period, they shouldn’t get the same text every time. For example, Quo won’t send another auto-reply to the same number within three hours.
4. **How easy is it to find missed calls that still need a response?** Missed calls can easily get buried when your team is busy. Filters can help you quickly see which customers still need a callback.

##


How to set up missed call text back software in Quo


If you want Quo to automatically text someone when you miss their call or text, you can set that up in just a few steps. Here’s how.


1. Open Quo and click **Settings** from the left-hand menu.


2. Select **Phone numbers** . If you have more than one number, choose the one you want to set the missed-call auto-reply for.


3. Tap **Automations** and scroll down to the **Auto-replies** section.


4. Under **During business hours** or **After business hours** , choose the trigger conditions for when you want to send auto-replies.


- If you only want to send a text when someone calls and doesn’t leave a voicemail, select **Set missed call (no voicemail) auto reply** .


- If you want to send a text when someone calls and leaves a voicemail, select **Set missed call (with voicemail) auto reply** .


- If you want to automatically send a text when someone messages, select **Set incoming message auto-reply.**


5. Type the message you want people to receive.


6. Click **Save** .


Once you save your changes, Quo will automatically send that text any time you miss a call. That way, callers get an update, even when your team can’t pick up the phone.

**FAQs**


****How does missed call text back software work?****


When your business phone number misses a call, it triggers your missed call text back software to send an automated message. Some systems allow you to customize this reply based on business hours, message type, or call frequency. Keep in mind that many phone systems, including Quo, include a missed call text back feature.


****Is there an app that will allow me to schedule text messages when replying to missed calls?****


You can use Quo to schedule text messages in your recipient’s time zones. That way, you won’t interrupt them outside of business hours or accidentally violate[TCPA requirements](https://www.quo.com/blog/tcpa-compliance-checklist/) .


**How do you text back a missed call with an iPhone or Android phone?**


The only way to send an[auto-reply text via iPhone](https://www.quo.com/blog/auto-reply-text-iphone/) is to use Driving Focus mode or the Shortcuts app. However, this is difficult to scale beyond two or three missed calls per month. If you run a growing small business, you’ll need a dedicated[missed call solution](https://www.quo.com/blog/missed-call-solution/) .
There’s no native[auto-reply feature on Android](https://www.quo.com/blog/auto-reply-text-android/) . However, you can get around this by using a third-party app like Quo.


****Can you automatically text back missed calls after business hours?****


Yes. In Quo, you can set up personalized auto-replies that send an[after-hours business text message](https://www.quo.com/blog/after-business-hours-text-message/) based on certain triggers. You can use this message to explain you’re out for the day but will be back on a certain date or at a certain time.


****Is there a free missed call text back software option?****


There are some free missed call text back apps for personal use. However, these are limited at best and not suitable for business use. It’s better to rely on business software like Quo if you plan on responding to missed business calls.


****What are the benefits of using missed call text back software?****


Missed call text back software helps you follow up instantly by sending a message the moment you miss a call. Here are a few ways it can help your business:


– Reassure callers you saw their call and will get back to them soon.
– Gather helpful information about what they need or when they’re free to talk.
– Ask for their name or order number so your team can follow up quickly.
– Reduce lost leads or opportunities when your team is tied up.


****What happens if a customer replies to the automated text?****


If you use a business phone system like Quo, any reply to your automated text will go straight to your team’s inbox. The message appears just like a normal text thread that your team can read and reply to.


****What should I text if I miss a call?****


A good missed call text is short, friendly, and sets clear expectations for when you’ll respond. For example, you can write, “Sorry we missed your call. We’ll reach out shortly.” You can also add another way to contact you if it helps, like your business hours or a link to book an appointment. This gives the caller a next step instead of waiting for one of your reps.


****How much does a missed call really cost?****


When a customer calls your business, there’s a reason. They might be ready to book an appointment, ask for a quote, or buy something. If no one answers, that potential revenue can disappear with the call. And many of those opportunities are lost: around[69% of missed business calls don’t get a callback](https://www.quo.com/blog/small-business-callback-statistics/) within 24 hours. But how much revenue could those missed calls actually cost *your* business? Enter your monthly call volume, average customer value, and close rate into[our missed call calculator](https://www.quo.com/tools/missed-call-cost-calculator) .


****How much does missed call text back software cost?****


Quo starts at $15 per user per month. That includes missed call text back software, plus unlimited calls and texts to US and Canadian numbers. As your business grows, your team can handle more customer conversations without running into usage limits.


****What are the most common missed call text back mistakes?****


A missed call text can keep the conversation going even when your team can’t pick up the phone. But what the text says can determine whether the customer replies or moves on.
Here are three mistakes to avoid:


– **Sending a message that doesn’t help:** “Sorry we missed you” doesn’t give the customer any useful information. Ask what they need help with so your team knows why they called.
– **Making the message too long:** Customers shouldn’t have to read a paragraph to understand your text. Keep it short and include only what they need to know.
– **Not saying when you’ll respond:** If no one can get back to them until tomorrow morning, tell them. That way, they know when to expect a response.
